item.title: Nagahama: Glass Studios in a Castle Town — Guide
item.description: Nagahama, the castle town Toyotomi Hideyoshi built as his first domain on Lake Biwa’s northeastern shore, has reinvented its historic core as one of Japan’s most successful heritage-revival districts. Its centrepiece is Kurokabe Square, named for the handsome ‘black wall’ Meiji-era bank building that now anchors a quarter of glass studios, galleries and workshops where artisans blow, cut and lamp-work glass before your eyes, threaded through streets of latticed townhouses, sake shops and the venerable Daitsuji temple, with Hideyoshi’s rebuilt lakeside castle keep watching from its park.

item.title: Shiga Top Sightseeing: Hikone Castle, Lake Biwa, and Beyond
item.description: Shiga Prefecture wraps around Lake Biwa, Japan’s largest lake, in the heart of the Kinki region just east of Kyoto. Despite its proximity to major tourism centres, it remains undervisited by foreign travellers — which makes it one of the most rewarding prefectures for those willing to look beyond the obvious. The highlights span feudal castle architecture, tranquil Edo-period gardens, sacred island pilgrimage, and lakeside shrine photography that rivals any scene in Japan.
